summary: VERIFIED: this is not a reimplementation of the RA2 engine. It is a v86 x86 emulator (BSD-2 v86 0.5.441, JIT to WASM) with custom boot firmware, a PE loader and a TypeScript Win32/DirectDraw/DirectSound/Winsock/DirectPlay/OLE compatibility layer. It runs Westwood's ORIGINAL binaries (RA2 1.006 game.exe in an XWIS-client build, YR 1.001 gamemd.exe) in the browser without booting Windows. All game logic, AI, rendering (the software DirectDraw blitter drawing SHP/VXL/TMP), palettes, house colours, audio mixing and Bink FMV decoding (the native Binkw32.dll) run inside the emulated x86 guest. The host receives only finished 800x600 to 1920x1080 frames (8-bit indexed + palette, or RGB565) and presents them with WebGL2. Code quality is high: GPL-3.0-or-later, strict layering, 918 asset-free tests passing, and the production build succeeded in about 11 s on this Mac. Fidelity for Step 1 is potentially perfect, because it IS the original game. It is weak for Step 2: the host cannot see objects, tiles, depth or water, so an HD remaster is limited to (a) whole-frame post-processing and AI upscaling, which already exists, (b) same-resolution repainted assets inside MIX files, or (c) a very large reverse-engineering effort to hook gamemd.exe draw routines and rebuild a host-side renderer. Legal caveat (VERIFIED in code): at page load it automatically downloads EA's copyrighted executables from a third-party host (oldgame.store). Its UI also links to unofficial game download sites. The patches are pinned to exact EXE SHA-256 hashes, so legally purchased EA App or Steam executables may not work (UNVERIFIED). The repo is only about 2 weeks old.

tech_stack: TypeScript 5.9 (tsc strict typecheck), React 19.3 (UI only), Vite 6.4.3, pnpm 11.24.0 workspace (strictDepBuilds), Vitest 4.1 and Playwright 1.60 for browser smoke tests. v86 0.5.441 (x86 emulator, WASM JIT enabled: disable_jit:false in src/adapter/vmCore.ts). The custom BIOS/boot firmware is NASM assembly (src/vm86/boot.asm -> boot.bin). 7z-wasm, fflate and a vendored LZMA-JS handle archives, including NSIS installers. onnxruntime-web 1.29.0 (WebGPU) is used only in dev-only experiments. Rendering is raw WebGL2 with a Canvas 2D fallback; no Three.js or WebGPU renderer. Audio is Web Audio via an AudioWorklet (src/adapter/pcmStreamWorklet.js). Execution runs in a Web Worker with a main-thread fallback. There is a Node WebSocket relay (packages/relay, ws, Docker compose). About 38k lines of TS/TSX in src/.
renderer_architecture: VERIFIED: the repo has NO asset-format code, meaning no MIX/SHP/VXL/HVA/TMP/PAL/CSF/INI parsers. grep finds these extensions only in src/games/shared/resourcePolicy.ts (a static-file regex for caching) and in custom-map filtering. The original gamemd.exe/game.exe inside v86 reads MIX files through the file shim (src/vm86/shim/stateFiles.ts, kernel32.ts). The engine's own software renderer then draws SHP sprites, software-rendered voxels, isometric TMP tiles, palettes, house-colour remaps, shroud/fog and lighting (the original tint/ambient model) into DirectDraw surfaces. Those surfaces are emulated in src/vm86/shim/directx.ts (IDirectDraw, IDirectDrawSurface Blt/BltFast/Flip/Lock, palettes) and src/vm86/shim/stateGraphics.ts. At present or flip time the shim emits a VmFrame (src/vm86/win32.ts:102): width/height, 8-bit `pixels` plus a 256-entry `palette`, or `rgb565`/`rgba`, plus a separate cursor bitmap. src/graphics/framePresenter.ts coalesces frames to the newest one. src/ui/pages/game/vmFrameRenderer.ts (createVmFrameRenderer) uploads an R8 index texture plus a palette texture and does the palette lookup in a GLSL ES 3.0 fragment shader, or uploads RGB565/RGBA directly. Its optional upscalers are bicubic, AMD FSR 1.0 EASU/RCAS (fsrUpscale.ts), ScaleFX (scalefxUpscale.ts), and Anime4K CNN/GAN 2x as GLSL (aiUpscale.ts, vendor/Anime4K_*.glsl). setPostProcess() provides a single-pass colour post-process host (src/graphics/framePostProcess.ts ColorPostProcess), used by the SweetFX Vibrance+LumaSharpen port (src/graphics/reshadePreset.ts). A dev-only WebGPU ONNX super-resolution path (experiments/liveModel.ts, modelProbe.ts) supports UltraSharpV2 Lite 4x, NomosUni SPAN 2x, AnimeSharpV2 and APISR, with input capped at 800x600. Camera, projection and lighting are all inside the original binary: the host has no depth, lighting or object information. Game resolution is set by patching RA2.INI/RA2MD.INI [Video] (src/games/resolution.ts), with a whitelist of 800x600 up to 1920x1080. Netcode: the original lockstep protocol runs unchanged. Winsock/IPX datagrams are mapped to virtual addresses (src/games/ra2/winsock.ts, networkTransport.ts) and carried over a room-based WebSocket relay (packages/relay, relayWire.ts), with a separate DirectPlay shim (dplayx.ts). Audio: DirectSound buffers are mixed and streamed to an AudioWorklet (src/adapter/audio.ts). Video: the native Bink 1.0p DLL runs in the guest, with small guest-DLL patches (src/games/ra2/profile.ts guestDllPatches).

build_result: SUCCESS. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` used pnpm v11.24.0 (switched automatically from the installed 11.5.2) and finished in about 15 s, with the lockfile supply-chain policy check passing. `pnpm run build` (relay lib build + tsc --noEmit for app and relay + vite build) finished in about 11 s. It produced dist/ at 6.1 MB, including v86.wasm (2.1 MB), 7zz.wasm (1.65 MB), vmWorker (743 kB) and page (871 kB). The only messages were warnings: node:crypto, node:fs/promises and module were externalized for the browser in v86/7z-wasm, plus the chunk-size >500 kB notice. `pnpm run test:unit` gave 128 test files and 918 tests, all passing, in 6 s. I did not run nasm (not installed; only needed for build:boot), the dev server, browser/real-game tests, or `prepare:third-party`. That last script downloads EA executables from a third-party host, which I deliberately avoided. No game assets were used.
feature_completeness: Every gameplay feature comes from the original executable, so in principle everything the retail game has exists. What the repo adds is emulation plumbing, and the verification status varies. Allied/Soviet campaigns: shim support exists (src/games/ra2/profile.ts campaignMenu handling; Maps01/02.mix listed as optional in manifest.ts). NOT regression-tested; the README says short regressions "do not establish compatibility with every campaign". Yuri's Revenge: VERIFIED as a supported target (src/games/yr/*, gamemd.exe 1.001 hash-pinned, MAPSMD03.MIX optional). YR campaign save policy is "retains its previous campaign policy until separately validated" (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). Skirmish vs AI: VERIFIED as the primary tested path, with a direct-to-skirmish startup hook (src/games/*/battleStartup.ts, startupPage.ts). AI quality is the original Westwood AI, unchanged. Online/LAN multiplayer: VERIFIED in code. The native LAN lobby runs over a WebSocket relay (src/games/ra2/winsock.ts, packages/relay). Only 2-player short matches are tested. There is no reconnect or resume (docs/RA2_NETWORK_RELIABILITY.md). All units, buildings, superweapons, naval, water, bridges, garrisoning, veterancy, Chronosphere and Iron Curtain: inherent to the original binary. Not individually tested; no code is needed. Fog and shroud: inherent. Custom maps: VERIFIED import of .yrm/.mpr from archives (src/adapter/customMapPackage.ts, CustomMapDialog.tsx). .csf is saved but not mounted; .map is not in the accepted list. Sound, EVA and music: VERIFIED via a DirectSound shim and AudioWorklet (src/adapter/audio.ts); Theme.mix/thememd.mix optional. FMV: VERIFIED by running the native Binkw32.dll in the guest with patches; movies are optional. Save/load: VERIFIED via the OLE IPersistStream shim and SGBYSTG1 container, with RA2 and YR save/cold-load real-game tests (tests/real-game/*/saveLoad.test.ts). Browser IndexedDB and campaign transitions are not covered. Replays: none (the original game has none). INI modding: top-level rules.ini/art.ini/ai.ini overrides and the "Mental Omega"-style... more precisely the Chinese mod 共和国之辉 (expand01/ecache01.mix, ra2.csf) are allowed (manifest.ts playerOptional). There is NO Ares/Phobos/Syringe support: grep finds none, and Syringe's debugger-based injection is not emulated. Map editor: none. Performance at high resolution: resolutions are capped at 1920x1080 (src/games/resolution.ts). Native logic-FPS diagnostics exist (docs/GAME_PERFORMANCE.md). I did not measure performance here (no assets); the issue #1 reporter called it very smooth on macOS. Extras: cheat-code UI, touch controls, keyboard lock, and English/Chinese UI.
asset_requirements: The player supplies files from a local folder or an archive (zip/7z/rar/NSIS installer; the extractor is in src/utils/archive). The result is cached in IndexedDB. RA2 required: ra2.mix, language.mix, Binkw32.dll, Blowfish.dll. YR required: ra2md.mix, langmd.mix, BINKW32.DLL, Blowfish.dll. The YR base-package notes are in docs/RESOURCE_PACKAGE_EVIDENCE.md; YR also needs the RA2 base layer (games/archivePolicy.ts). Optional: Maps01/02.mix, movies01/02.mix, Multi.mix, Theme.mix, Taunts/, subtitle.txt, game.fnt, and mod overrides for RA2; expandmd01.mix, MAPSMD03.MIX, movmd03.mix, MULTIMD.MIX, thememd.mix and subtitlemd.txt for YR. The executables are NOT taken from the player. game.exe (sha256 06f99496...ccdb, an RA2 1.006 XWIS-client build) and gamemd.exe (sha256 7b8a0685...94b6, YR 1.001) are fetched from https://oldgame.store/ and overlaid on the player's files (src/ui/pages/game/gameSourcePicker.ts:115-121). All compatibility patches and hooks check these exact hashes (src/games/ra2/startupPage.ts, src/games/yr/startupPage.ts). The UI's download dialog points to third-party game packages. For a clean project, the user should supply files from their own legal copy, e.g. the EA App / Steam "Command & Conquer Red Alert 2 and Yuri's Revenge" (Steam app 2229850). Whether those executables match the pinned hashes is UNVERIFIED. If they do not, every address-specific patch in src/games/ra2 and src/games/yr would need re-derivation.
hd_extensibility:
Core limitation (VERIFIED): the host only sees final composited frames (VmFrame in src/vm86/win32.ts). docs/RESHADE_ADAPTATION.md says: "Final frames alone cannot reproduce plugin water, occlusion, or layered high-resolution drawing." Options by difficulty:
(1) EASY, days: post-processing and upscaling of the final frame. Hook points: src/ui/pages/game/vmFrameRenderer.ts (setUpscaleMode, setPostProcess), src/graphics/framePostProcess.ts (ColorPostProcess, single pass; would need a multipass/FBO chain), src/graphics/reshadePreset.ts, and src/ui/pages/game/experiments/liveModel.ts (WebGPU ONNX full-frame SR, dev-only, 800x600 input cap). You get sharpening, colour grading, FSR, Anime4K/ESRGAN-style SR, film grain, vignette, and screen-space rain/snow overlays. Limits: it also affects the sidebar and UI, has no depth or occlusion (rain falls in front of buildings), shows temporal flicker from AI SR on pixel art, and cannot produce real water reflections, dynamic lights or modern explosions.
(2) MEDIUM, weeks to months of art work: asset-level replacement inside MIX files (repainted SHP/VXL/TMP, new palettes, new animation SHPs, art.ini tweaks). The original engine loads these through the existing overlay mechanism (manifest.ts playerOptional expand/ecache MIX, OverlayGameFileProvider in src/resources/providers/overlay.ts). But the engine draws at a fixed 1:1 pixel scale on 60x30 iso cells, so there is no pixel-density gain. Voxels stay software-rendered, and effects are limited to what SHP animations and the original lighting can do. External Windows-era tools (XCC, OS SHP Builder) would be needed; none are in the repo.
(3) VERY HARD, many months to years: a guest draw-command bridge like Toumao's ReShade plugin (strings found: AnimClass_Draw_SetTexture, TechnoClass_RenderVxl_ReplaceMesh, GScreenClass_Update_TransferBuffer). It would reuse the hook pattern in src/games/yr/spawnerProbe.ts and GameRuntimeHooks.prepareImage (src/games/runtimeHooks.ts): hash-checked trampolines patched into guest memory. Those trampolines would export per-frame object, tile, Z-buffer, shroud and water masks through new hypercalls and VmFrame fields. A brand-new host WebGL2/WebGPU compositor in src/graphics/ would then draw HD sprites, voxel-to-mesh models with normal/depth lighting, water shaders and GPU particles, while the guest draw is suppressed. This needs YRpp-level reverse engineering of exact gamemd.exe/game.exe builds, done separately for RA2 and YR. It adds cross-thread bandwidth cost in the Worker and fights the project's own rule against game-specific code in vm86. It amounts to writing a new renderer driven by emulated game state. The repo documents only a LaserBlit passthrough experiment (src/graphics/experimental/reshadeLaser.ts) and no data bridge.
Summary: good for "original plus filters"; structurally poor for a "2026-level 2.5D HD remaster".
risks: LEGAL, high: the app automatically downloads EA's copyrighted game.exe/gamemd.exe from a third-party host (https://oldgame.store) on page load (src/main.ts preloadThirdPartyFiles; src/games/manifest.ts). Its download catalog (src/games/downloadCatalog.ts) links to unofficial game download sites. A derivative that keeps this redistributes, or facilitates redistribution of, unlicensed EA binaries. EA has not open-sourced RA2/YR.

Hash lock-in: every patch and hook is pinned to one specific RA2 1.006 XWIS-build game.exe and one YR 1.001 gamemd.exe. It is unverified whether the user's legally purchased EA App/Steam executables match. If they do not, the patches must be re-derived by disassembly.

Architectural mismatch with Step 2: rendering happens inside the emulated original binary. The host only gets final 2D frames, so crisp HD materials, modern water, realistic weather and modern impact effects cannot be added without a massive reverse-engineering bridge and a new host renderer.
The original engine has a fixed pixel scale and a resolution whitelist capped at 1920x1080 (src/games/resolution.ts). On a 3456x2234 display, higher resolution means seeing more map, not sharper art.
Emulation performance ceiling: x86 runs in the v86 WASM JIT. Any extra per-frame hooks or data export compete with emulation throughput. I did not measure performance on the M5 Pro (no assets).
No Ares/Phobos/Syringe support, which rules out the modern YR modding ecosystem that community HD/graphics enhancements rely on.

Project maturity: Alpha, public for about 2 weeks. The real history is on a private dev branch with squashed public drops, which makes long-term upstream merging and provenance auditing harder. Two GitHub-linked contributors, with heavy AI-agent authorship.
Campaigns (especially YR campaign saves) and long or 4-8 player matches are explicitly not regression-validated. Multiplayer has no reconnect.

GPL-3.0-or-later copyleft: any distributed derivative must be GPL. Some assets (the startup background) have unclear licensing per docs/THIRD_PARTY.md. The AI SR model weights referenced in the docs are CC BY-NC-SA and must not ship.
Minor: UI CSS openly imitates Chrono Divide's page styles (styles.css comments). Low risk but worth removing for cleanliness.
score_rationale:
Strengths: Step 1 fidelity is unmatched, because this runs the real game (units, AI, campaigns, YR, lockstep MP and FMV all come from the original code). Code quality is excellent: clean layering, 918 passing tests, and a build in seconds. The GPL-3.0-or-later licence on the project code is unambiguous. There is no Chrono Divide derivation. It already ships frame-level upscaling (FSR, Anime4K, ONNX SR) and a post-process hook.
Weaknesses for THIS project: (a) The user's core goal is a 2.5D HD remaster with crisper materials, modern water, weather and impact effects. That needs control of the renderer, which this architecture structurally withholds: everything is drawn by the emulated 2000-era binary into a fixed-scale framebuffer. Beyond filters and upscaling, the only path is a years-scale hook-and-rebuild effort that is effectively a new renderer. (b) Legally, the default runtime pulls EA executables from a third-party mirror, and patches are hash-locked to those exact builds. A clean derivative must strip this and may not work with legitimately purchased executables. (c) It is two weeks old, in Alpha, with squashed private-branch development.
Net: roughly 8/10 as a "play original RA2 in the browser" or reference/oracle base, but roughly 2/10 as a foundation for the HD remaster. Weighted for this two-step project: 4/10. Best uses: a Step 1 playable reference, a fidelity oracle for behaviour comparison, and a quick "HD-lite" via its existing post-process and upscale stack. It is not the renderer foundation for Step 2.
